item.title: Can AI Generate Good Designs from Raw User Data?
item.content:encoded: In our study, AI-generated designs were better when the AI received synthesized findings and recommendations instead of raw user comments alone.

item.title: Journey Mapping 101
item.content:encoded: A journey map is a visualization of the process that a person goes through in order to accomplish a goal.

item.title: Research-In-The-Loop: How UXR Adapts to Development at AI Speed
item.content:encoded: As AI speeds up development, it can be a challenge for research to adapt. Research can define what each release must measure and what it can help teams discover.

item.title: Agent Harness: Definition
item.content:encoded: An agent harness manages a software loop between an AI model and its tools. Its context, permissions, and limits shape what users can do.

item.title: Usability 101: Introduction to Usability
item.content:encoded: Usability refers to how easily people can complete tasks with a design. Improve it by watching representative users do realistic tasks, early and repeatedly.

item.title: The Role of UX in Agentic Software Factories
item.content:encoded: AI-native software development lifecycles reduce UX to AI context. UX must discover user needs, shape what’s built, and evaluate it before and after launch.

item.title: Experience Design: Dropping the “User” from “User Experience”
item.content:encoded: AI is expanding UX beyond human users to agents acting on their behalf. Experience design names this broader field, which still centers on people’s goals.

item.title: AI in UX: Work Is Faster, But Practitioners Have Mixed Feelings
item.content:encoded: AI saves UX practitioners time on nearly every task, yet most feel lukewarm about it: mandates, unreliable output, and inflated expectations eat the gains.

item.title: Synthetic Users vs. Human Respondents: Same Conclusion, Less Variation
item.content:encoded: Data from AI-generated respondents pointed to the same conclusion as a survey of 604 humans but contained far fewer distinct answers.

item.title: The New Siri’s Biggest Strength Is Not Intelligence
item.content:encoded: A useful AI assistant needs relevant personal context, the capability to use it, and an experience that helps users understand its limits.

item.title: Context Libraries: How AI Power Users Manage Context Engineering
item.content:encoded: Claude power users rarely edit their context files and often can’t find them. Your AI agent is only as powerful as its context library.

item.title: Empathy Mapping: The First Step in Design Thinking
item.content:encoded: Empathy maps help UX teams visualize user attitudes and behaviors, building a shared understanding of end users while highlighting gaps in existing user data.

item.title: The New Big Ball of Mud: Why Agentic AI Systems Turn Fragile
